feature: The capture toast says how to open the editor
summary: After a capture the toast now carries an Edit row under the picture with the key, Shift Command 6, at its end. Before, the way into the editor was a pencil that only appeared on hover, a double-click, or a key only the Welcome window mentioned.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. The flag Edit from the capture toast is on by default; turn it off there to compare with the hover-only toast.

try.do: Press Shift Command 4 and drag over any part of the screen.
Look at the toast at the bottom right without moving the pointer to it. Read what it offers.
Click the Edit row. The capture opens in an editor and the toast leaves.
Capture again and hover the toast. Only Dismiss appears in the top corner now; the pencil is gone because Edit is already on screen.
Capture again, let the toast fade, then press Shift Command 6. The same capture opens.
Open Experiments, turn off Edit from the capture toast, and capture once more. The toast is back to the caption only, with the pencil on hover.
Record a short clip with Shift Command 5 and stop it. The recording toast has the same Edit row under its longer message.

evaluate: On a first capture, is the Edit row the first thing you would click, or does the toast still read as a receipt?
Does the key at the end of the row teach Shift Command 6 for later, or is it clutter you would rather lose?
Is the toast now too tall for something that fades on its own, or does the extra row earn its space?
Should the row say Edit, or something that names the destination, like Open in Editor?
rough: The pictures are offscreen renders of a mirror of the toast, not the running app: the loop cannot record the screen, so no capture could be made to trigger the real toast.

Edit and its key are in one full-width pill rather than a small button beside the caption. Beside the caption the footer measured 213 points against a 196 point picture, and the recording messages overflow even without the key.
On a Touch Bar Mac where macOS still owns Shift Command 6 the key is left off the row, so the toast never promises a key that does nothing. That case was not tried on a real Touch Bar machine.
The audit's original option of a hint line saying double-click to edit was not built: it teaches a gesture instead of offering the action, and double-click still works either way.
